intent: Whether a Heritage Hills homeowner can put artificial turf in a front or street-visible side yard, and how the community's own hardscape limit affects a back-yard putting green or turf area with paver surrounds or a sport-court pad.
distinctValue: The page already explains that Colorado's SB23-178 protects back-yard turf on a detached single-family home but leaves the front yard to the HOA. This adds the Heritage Hills HOA's own published design standard for that front-yard call: artificial turf is barred on front yards and on side yards visible from the street, effective 1 June 2022 and not retroactive, and hardscape (including sport courts) is capped at 20% of the front or back yard, excluding pool decking, with a discretionary path to 33% only when the landscape plan uses screening or the lot is enclosed by a privacy fence.

sources.label: Heritage Hills HOA: Design Standards
supports: Artificial turf is not permitted on front yards or side yards where visible from the street (Landscaping section, effective June 1, 2022)
Use of hardscape (e.g., concrete, tile, stone, sport courts) is limited to twenty percent (20%) of the area of the front/back yard
Pool decking is not included in this limitation.
may be expanded to a maximum of 33% if landscape screening has been employed in the landscape plan, or if the property is screened with a privacy fence
Effective Date: June 1, 2022 (not applied retroactively to projects completed or approved before this date)
